A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, and all supplied text, equations, figures and tables are readable. Both end with references on page 10; neither includes the cited supplementary derivation and additional experimental material, limiting comparison of those parts.

before.justification: v1 reports original velocity-estimation results on four real-world sequences, robot-arm and IMU comparisons, and runtime measurements in Section 6.

after.justification: v4 retains the original velocity-estimation experiments and application examples, and reports revised error distributions and runtime summaries.

M1.justification: The SegNeXt flow/depth network, training losses, differentiable least-squares solver and photometric direction-selection procedure are retained. Expanded explanations of coordinates and warping do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both use ScanNet++-derived synthetic data, collected indoor images, the same four test sequences, and robot-arm and IMU examples. v4 clarifies indoor scope and unseen test scenes; GoPro is discussed but explicitly excluded from evaluation.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain COLMAP with SIFT/AdaLAM or DISK/LightGlue, MASt3R, DROID-SLAM, the zero-velocity baseline and IMU integration. The zero-velocity baseline newly discussed in v4 already appears in v1 Tables 1–2; newly cited related methods are not benchmarked.

E3.justification: Table 3 changes from billiards-only runtime and realtime factors to average FPS across test sequences, excluding failed COLMAP reconstructions. Figure 5 also changes from billiards-only to aggregate error distributions. The main accuracy metrics and stated training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 5 expands the error-distribution analysis from billiards to all already evaluated test sequences, and Figure 4 revises the illustrative velocity comparison. The robot-arm and IMU case studies remain; additional sequence plots cited in the missing supplement cannot be checked.

E5.justification: v4 Table 3 newly specifies averaging three timing runs per sequence. v1 gives no timing-run count, so this does not establish an increase in runs. No confidence intervals or significance tests are added to the supplied results.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their RMSE values and rankings. Figure 4 changes the plotted COLMAP trajectories, Figure 5 reports different aggregate CDFs, and Table 3 replaces single-sequence timings with cross-sequence FPS, including 30.17 FPS for the proposed method. These runtime summaries do not establish a same-setting speed improvement.

T1.justification: The printed motion-field equations, losses and least-squares solution remain equivalent; v1 Equation 17 is retained inline in v4 Section 5.1. Both versions refer the derivation to supplementary material absent from the supplied PDFs, preventing a reliable comparison of that formal reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: IMU-like velocity estimation from motion blur, synthetic-to-real training, robustness to aggressive motion, state-of-the-art accuracy and real-time operation. Changing contribution wording from relative-pose estimates to velocity estimates clarifies the existing objective.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly limits the study to indoor scenes, anticipates weaker outdoor performance, and states that rolling shutter and nonuniform intra-exposure motion are not modeled. It also explains the ARKit body-frame ground-truth choice and qualifies the IMU comparison as direct velocity versus integrated acceleration.

D1.justification: v4 adds centered-coordinate and backward-flow details and clarifies unseen test scenes, varying exposures and body-frame velocity evaluation. Section 5.1 corrects the stated interpolated-frame count from N+(N−1) to 2N+1, although Figure 3 retains the old label; this does not demonstrate a changed implementation.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands coverage of single-frame rotational and translational motion estimation, including Klein and Drummond and Boracchi, and discusses Zhao et al.'s full-pose method requiring clean depth. A new Deblurring discussion positions the work against joint depth, motion and deblurring approaches, substantially improving coverage of closely related research.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, dataset description and experimental narrative undergo extensive rewriting and compression. Direction disambiguation receives a fuller explanation and related work gains a Deblurring subsection, while the main section sequence remains intact.

P2.justification: Figures 4–5 are redrawn or reformatted, Figure 3 changes column placement, and Figure 7 moves within the redesigned page 8 layout. Table 3 replaces runtime/realtime-factor columns with FPS. The overall two-column format and seven-figure, three-table structure remain.

improvement.justification: v4 improves research context, applicability boundaries and evaluation transparency through closer prior-work comparisons, explicit limitations, aggregate error analysis and documented timing repetitions. Core accuracy evidence remains unchanged. The gains are limited by retained blanket claims that no prior single-image methods exist despite the expanded related work, unexplained trajectory revisions, and unavailable supplementary material.
